hed: Boston judge’s PI keeps DHS student/journalist visa-duration rule off as Sept. 15 start hits
dek: U.S. District Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV’s Monday preliminary injunction postponing the effective date of DHS’s final rule ending “duration of status” for F, J, and I nonimmigrants remained in force Tuesday morning — the day the four-year student/exchange and 240-day journalist caps were set to begin. The order bars implementation pending further proceedings, with a status conference set for Oct. 2; higher-ed and labor plaintiffs had argued the fixed-term regime and unappealable extension denials were arbitrary under the APA.

byline: Event summary from public reporting and named outlets

cl.body: Reuters’s Monday Boston wrap, AFP’s Tuesday follow, and Fragomen’s practitioner alert cast Tuesday as the non-start that campuses and newsrooms sought: Saylor postponed the Sept. 15 effective date and enjoined implementation, noting discretionary, unappealable extension denials and national-security rationales that the court called thin — leaving F/J/I duration-of-status admissions in place for now.

cr.body: DHS’s July final-rule release (Secretary Markwayne Mullin), The Washington Times’ Monday court write-through, and the Washington Examiner’s duration-of-status defense frame the rule as closing a decades-old open-ended stay that let some F/J/I holders avoid routine federal re-vetting — arguing fixed admissions plus USCIS extensions restore temporary-visa integrity even as a Bush-appointed judge pauses the Sept. 15 start pending appeal options.

stack_blurb: Saylor PI still bars DHS F/J/I duration-of-status end on planned Sept. 15 start.
seo_description: Boston Judge F. Dennis Saylor IV issued a preliminary injunction Monday blocking DHS’s rule ending duration of status for foreign students, exchange visitors, and journalists.
